key_insight: A hybrid FTA-DEMATEL-EC framework reveals that the most frequent ultrasonic welding failures are not always the most costly, so reliability priorities should be based on both causality and economic impact.
engineering_relevance: For high-volume ultrasonic welding lines, the framework helps managers target root causes, reduce scrap, and prevent rare but expensive equipment damage through better maintenance and setup control.
method: FTA estimated failure probabilities for the Branson 2000X AED welding system.
DEMATEL traced hidden cause-effect relationships among failure sources.
Expected Cost (EC) ranked risks by financial impact, not just occurrence.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports component defects (25.9%) and process instability (24.0%) as the most frequent failures, while inefficient maintenance budgeting emerged as the main root cause and human setup/handling errors as the highest-cost risk.
watch_item: The framework depends on quality failure data and cost estimates, so results may shift if reporting is incomplete or if plant-specific operating conditions differ.
paper_title: Improving the reliability of ultrasonic welding: a hybrid FTA-DEMATEL-EC framework for cost and risk prioritization in mass production
